headline: Autonomous AI turned decisively offensive as Palo Alto Networks' NOVA system surfaced more than 14,000 open-source vulnerabilities while misconfigured AI agents spilled secrets from meeting rooms to code repositories.

emerging_trends.text: Palo Alto Networks' NOVA system and the rise of vibe hacking show frontier AI collapsing the gap between attacker skill and offensive reach, letting almost anyone industrialize zero-day discovery.
Weak defaults and prompt injection turned AI helpers into liabilities, as a tl;dv Firebase flaw exposed private meetings and Google pulled three ADK workflows that a rogue GitHub issue could hijack.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agents and Assistants Spill Secrets

emerging_trends.text: Social engineering outran technical controls as device-code phishing jumped 1,500% and adversaries hosted lures on Cloudflare Workers and Vercel to slip past multifactor authentication.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Social Engineering and MFA-Bypass Phishing Surge

topics.title: Social Engineering and MFA-Bypass Phishing Surge
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported device-code phishing rose 1,500% and vishing doubled across 2026, Kaspersky detailed adversary-in-the-middle phishing that abuses Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, and IPFS to bypass multifactor authentication, and fresh scams impersonate American Express with a fake child-exploitation accusation and the IRS with bogus Digital Asset Compliance Portal letters.
topics.summary: Attackers lean on social engineering and legitimate cloud hosting to defeat MFA and entrenched controls while leaving little evidence; consumers face fake fraud calls and crypto-tax letters designed to panic them into paying.

sources.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
How legitimate cloud platforms enable phishers to bypass MFA
"Your Credit Card Has Been Used In A Crime" Scam Spreads
Fake IRS letters target cryptocurrency holders

topics.title: AI Agents and Assistants Spill Secrets
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading found a Google Firebase misconfiguration in the tl;dv meeting notetaker that lets any user query other users' meetings and join their calls, Google deleted three workflows from its Agent Development Kit after Pillar Security showed a malicious GitHub issue could trigger a privileged code-fixing agent, and SecurityWeek detailed weaponized email AI assistants that impersonate employees and hijack executive accounts.
topics.summary: Built-in AI assistants and agent frameworks leak data and privileged actions through weak defaults and prompt injection; affected products span tl;dv, Google's ADK, and email chatbots, so buyers must govern agent permissions like human accounts.

sources.title: AI Notetaker Lets Hackers Spy on Government, Corporate Video Calls
Google Deletes 3 ADK AI Workflows After Malicious GitHub Issue Could Trigger Privileged Agent
Weaponized Email AI Assistants Could Help Attackers Hijack Accounts

topics.title: Frontier AI Industrializes Zero-Day Discovery
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 ran its NOVA system across the open-source software supply chain and surfaced more than 14,000 previously unknown vulnerabilities, while The Hacker News described the shift to vibe hacking that turns frontier models into a tireless junior hacker for any adversary.
topics.summary: Autonomous AI now finds and exploits software flaws at industrial scale, severing the old link between attacker expertise and offensive capability and flooding defenders with findings faster than they can patch.

sources.title: The Frontier AI Vulnerability Burst: Industrializing Autonomous Zero-Day Discovery in Open-Source Software
When Vibe Hacking Turns AI into the Junior Hacker Every Adversary Always Wanted

topics.title: TP-Link Omada and cPanel Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Forescout disclosed 15 new vulnerabilities in TP-Link's Omada networking ecosystem whose zero-touch-provisioning chain hands attackers full network takeover, and cPanel patched CVE-2026-58048, a 9.4-rated flaw that let an authenticated hosting customer run SQL as the database root.
topics.summary: Fresh chains in widely deployed network gear and hosting control panels cross privilege boundaries that separate customers from administrators; operators should apply the TP-Link Omada and cPanel updates now.

sources.title: TP-Link Omada ZTP Vulnerabilities Chain Into Full Network Takeover
New cPanel Critical Flaw Could Let Hosting Customers Run SQL as Database Root

topics.title: Swiss Federal IT Agency Breach
topics.latest_developments: Switzerland's Federal Office for Information Technology and Communications, the BIT, said its specialists detected anomalies on on-premises Microsoft servers and that intruders compromised roughly 200 accounts, with SharePoint vulnerabilities the suspected entry point.
topics.summary: The BIT runs shared IT for Swiss federal agencies and could not confirm how the hackers got in. Organizations running on-premises SharePoint should patch immediately and hunt for signs of compromise.

sources.title: Swiss IT agency hacked, 200 accounts compromised, SharePoint vulns suspected

topics.title: Apple Fights UK iCloud Access Demand
topics.latest_developments: Apple is mounting a new legal challenge to British demands for a way around its Advanced Data Protection feature, seeking to keep users' end-to-end encrypted iCloud accounts closed to the government.
topics.summary: The United Kingdom has pressed Apple for backdoor access to encrypted iCloud data through a technical capability notice; Apple's renewed challenge tests how far a government can compel a company to weaken encryption.

sources.title: Apple launches new legal challenge against UK over iCloud access

business_politics.title: Bessent Says Strait of Hormuz Deal Is Near
business_politics.latest_developments: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said an Iran-Oman arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping is imminent and Brent crude fell 4%, even as a fresh strike on a cargo ship in the strait left the opening in doubt.
business_politics.summary: Iranian and Omani negotiators reached a temporary arrangement to restore tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint for roughly a fifth of the world's oil, easing a war now in its sixth month; Saudi Aramco posted a $33 billion quarterly profit on elevated crude prices.

sources.title: Oil falls after Bessent says deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz is imminent
Hormuz Opening Uncertain After New Strike
Saudi Aramco's Bumper $33 Billion Profit Gives Kingdom's Finances a Boost

business.title: Wayfair to Open First Pennsylvania Store
business.latest_developments: Wayfair will open its first Pennsylvania store, a 95,000-square-foot showroom, at the North Hills Village shopping center on McKnight Road in 2027.
business.summary: The online furniture retailer Wayfair picked Pittsburgh's North Hills for its first physical store in the state, a 95,000-square-foot space along McKnight Road that the company will organize by room and style.

sources.title: Wayfair opening North Hills store, will be company's first Pennsylvania location

around_town.title: Federal Funding Expands EV Charging in Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: Pennsylvania's small towns will receive the newest wave of federal funding to build electric-vehicle charging stations, the Post-Gazette reported.
around_town.summary: A fresh round of federal money will install electric-vehicle chargers in small towns across Pennsylvania, extending the state's charging network beyond its cities.

around_teams.title: Young Steelers Starters Bank on Continuity
around_teams.latest_developments: Returning offensive starters told the Post-Gazette that keeping the same nucleus around quarterback Aaron Rodgers should pay off in 2026.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette reported that younger Steelers offensive starters, tight end Pat Freiermuth, tackle Troy Fautanu, guard Mason McCormick, and center Zach Frazier among them, believe a stable core around Aaron Rodgers will lift the offense this season.

around_teams.title: Jaquan Brisker Comes Home to the Steelers
around_teams.latest_developments: Safety Jaquan Brisker told the Post-Gazette he is settling in with his hometown Steelers after four seasons with the Chicago Bears, and his family packed the training-camp stands.
around_teams.summary: Gateway High School and Penn State safety Jaquan Brisker, signed by Pittsburgh after four years with the Chicago Bears, said 'I'm actually a Steeler' as his family filled the Saint Vincent College camp stands to welcome the Western Pennsylvania native home.

sources.title: Pittsburgh native Jaquan Brisker called his shot and landed in the NFL. Now, 'I'm actually a Steeler.'

reading.summary: Ben Thompson reads Microsoft's strong quarter as a sign of strategic clarity, lower costs, and tangible AI applications, and argues the reasons behind that efficiency payoff are more unsettling than they first appear.

reading.title: Premium: AI Is Getting Way Too Expensive
reading.summary: Zitron argues that the actual cost of running large language models is climbing fast enough to undercut the industry's theoretical claims about productivity gains and displaced jobs.
